lines.name: Island Line

segments.routing: Open unzoned bay; slow only in Bear Cut shore buffers, the 100-yd Rickenbacker bridge pocket, and the last 0.5–1 nm at Brickell. Route AROUND the year-round no-entry zone west of Virginia Key — never cross it.

lines.phase_notes: Flagship — the strongest single corridor found in any city scanned to date. ~6 nm ≈ 20–25 min, foil-credible year-round, vs 80–90 min crisis-era Rickenbacker drives on the island's only road. Crandon is park-&-ride ($181.5K median HH income catchment); the entire Brickell finance cluster is within 12 min of the Vice City dock. Time claim (20–25 min) is whitelisted.

lines.name: Grove Line

segments.routing: Open bay with 1000-ft slow-speed shore buffers at each end; ~4.5–5 nm.

segments.water_min_label: indicative — subject to local speed zones
segments.constraint: Slow-speed all year around Brickell Key + river-mouth idle/slow zone on the EPIC approach (short hop)
segments.routing: Bayside only — EPIC's bay face; never enter the Miami River (idle all year + drawbridge curfews).

lines.phase_notes: Dinner Key ↔ Brickell in 15–20 min (foil-credible year-round; time claim whitelisted for this leg only) with City Hall + Grove offices southbound as reverse-commute demand. The short EPIC extension is the second Brickell gate serving the Flagler St downtown edge — that hop is speed-constrained and gets NO time claim.

lines.name: Beach Line

segments.routing: MANDATORY: exit Miami Beach Marina through the Government Cut RNA slow water (~0.5–1 nm), then via NORRIS CUT to open bay at speed. NEVER route via Fisherman's Channel (USCG slow RNA). No geometry through or over Fisher Island.

lines.phase_notes: SoFi premium catchment to Brickell finance jobs, ~5.5 nm ≈ 20–25 min via Norris Cut (foil-credible with routing care; time claim whitelisted). Complements — does not fight — the city's free Sunset Harbour↔Venetian water taxi.

lines.name: North Bay Line

segments.routing: Designated 30/35-mph channels and unzoned mid-bay water; idle pockets at the 79th St bridge.

segments.water_min_label: indicative — subject to local speed zones
segments.constraint: Downtown ICW channel is IDLE SPEED all year from 100 yd N of Venetian Cswy to the southern tip of Brickell Key — fixed slow tail into downtown

lines.phase_notes: Uses the 30/35-mph mid-bay water; accepts the idle tail into downtown. Pelican↔Venetian leg is time-claim eligible (30-mph ICW whitelist); the downtown tail renders indicative only.

lines.name: Gold Coast Line

segments.routing: 30-mph all-year ICW segments + unzoned mid-bay; several bridge idle pockets.

segments.water_min_label: indicative — subject to local speed zones
segments.constraint: Downtown ICW channel idle-speed all year (Venetian Cswy → Brickell Key) — fixed slow tail

lines.phase_notes: Bal Harbour/Surfside/Sunny Isles condo corridor to Venetian/Downtown. Haulover leg time-claim eligible (30-mph ICW whitelist); downtown tail indicative only. Bill Bird construction status must be verified before this line is promoted (internal).

lines.name: Bay Line

segments.routing: Same crossing as the live city water taxi: designated 30/35-mph channels through the Venetian basin (slow-except-as-designated water).

lines.phase_notes: Overlay/extension of the city's PROVEN 20-min crossing (free Miami Beach Water Taxi, live since Jan 2026, weekdays 7:00–19:30). Copy may cite the city service's 20-minute crossing as public proof; NO Navier time claim for this line until geometry seals (not on the foil-credible whitelist). Requires a City of Miami Beach dock agreement at Maurice Gibb (internal only).

lines.name: Aventura Seasonal Extension

segments.water_min_label: indicative — subject to local speed zones
segments.constraint: ICW channel through Sunny Isles/Dumbfoundling Bay is slow-speed Nov 15–Apr 30 (30 mph only May 1–Nov 14, 68C-22.025(1)(b)2) — service runs summer season ONLY

lines.phase_notes: Summer-season-only extension of the Gold Coast Line, and the label must say why: the ICW channel itself drops to slow speed Nov 15–Apr 30, so foil service is not viable in winter. This is a regulatory season, NOT a resort/summer-premium product — do not copy Hamptons framing. Revisit if the pending Miami-Dade MPP update changes the winter rule.

lines.name: Hollywood Commuter

segments.water_min_label: indicative — subject to local speed zones
segments.constraint: Port Everglades: slow-speed in ALL port waters year-round (~1.5 nm transit) + 6,000-ft ICW idle zone Nov 15–Mar 31; Hollywood ICW channel otherwise 25 mph all year
segments.routing: ICW channel; transit the Port Everglades entrance channel at posted speed (security-sensitive port — internal).

segments.water_min_label: indicative — subject to local speed zones
segments.constraint: New River slow-speed all year — final ~2 nm into downtown is a fixed ~20–25 min crawl
segments.routing: ICW to New River junction, then upriver past the 3rd Ave and Andrews Ave drawbridges (opening-rule schedule risk — internal open item).

lines.phase_notes: Hollywood Beach ↔ 17th St ↔ downtown Riverwalk, ~35–45 min end-to-end, competitive at peak — but every leg is speed-constrained, so ALL times render indicative. Existing docks at every stop. The commuter AM window (6:30–9:30) is genuinely unserved: the incumbent Water Taxi FTL runs leisure hours (10:00–22:00). Line name deliberately 'Hollywood Commuter' — 'Hollywood Express' is the incumbent's brand.

lines.name: Isles Shuttle

segments.water_min_label: indicative — subject to local speed zones
segments.constraint: New River slow-speed all year on the downtown approach; short ICW hop otherwise
segments.routing: ICW south from Bahia Mar to the New River junction, then upriver to the Riverwalk city docks.

lines.phase_notes: Short, slow-water, schedule-certainty product: beach/isles residents to Las Olas offices. Sells on reliability and a guaranteed seat, NOT speed — no time claims. Positioning: commuter-hours complement to Water Taxi FTL, potentially using their docks under agreement (internal).

lines.name: Pompano Line

segments.water_min_label: indicative — subject to local speed zones
segments.constraint: Year-round slow-speed minimum-wake BRA in the ICW between Oakland Park Blvd and Sunrise Blvd bridges (FWC, Nov 2025) + bridge idle pockets; ICW otherwise 25 mph on weekdays (winter-weekday rule-text verification open)

segments.water_min_label: indicative — subject to local speed zones
segments.constraint: New River slow-speed all year on the downtown approach
segments.routing: ICW to New River junction, then upriver.

lines.phase_notes: Phase-2 growth feeder from the Pompano/Lighthouse Point residential catchment to downtown FTL jobs. Budget the Oakland Park↔Sunrise slow pinch on every run; resolve the Broward winter-weekday ICW rule conflict (68C-22.010 F.A.C.) before scheduling. No time claims.

copy.hero_headline: Key Biscayne to Brickell in 20–25 minutes — instead of an 80–90 minute causeway crawl.
copy.hero_sub: Key Biscayne to Brickell in 20–25 minutes — instead of an 80–90 minute causeway crawl. Navier is building an employer water network for South Florida: 20-seat electric hydrofoils linking Key Biscayne, Coconut Grove, and South Beach to a dock two minutes from Brickell's towers, plus a second network connecting Hollywood Beach and the Las Olas Isles to downtown Fort Lauderdale.
copy.hero_note: Non-binding letter of intent · first service no earlier than end-2027 · two independent networks (no Miami↔FTL boat)
copy.hero_cta_network: Find a route to my office
copy.problem_title: Jobs on the water. Commutes in traffic.
copy.problem_lead: Miami's jobs sit on the water and its commutes sit in traffic. Brickell — the densest finance cluster in the Southeast — is a two-minute walk from an existing marina, and Key Biscayne's only road home has meant 80–90 minute drives. Miami Beach already runs a commuter water taxi — a free city service crossing the bay in a consistent 20 minutes since January 2026. We make it a network: more corridors, commuter frequency, and guaranteed employer seats.

problem_chips.label: Typical Key Biscayne → Brickell causeway crawl
Miami and Fort Lauderdale stay independent

copy.stripe_lesson: We ran the first employer water commute on San Francisco Bay. South Florida already proved the water works.

copy.proof_worked_body: Free city water taxi on the Beach corridor since Jan 2026; Water Taxi FTL owns leisure 10:00–22:00 — we complement commuter hours.
copy.proof_fixed_body: First employer water commute on SF Bay — twenty-seat class is the product.
copy.proof_ask_body: Non-binding LOI — seats or line anchor — so we sequence on real demand.
copy.network_lead: Three launch lines converge on Brickell: the Island Line (Key Biscayne ↔ Brickell, 20–25 min), the Grove Line (Coconut Grove ↔ Brickell, 15–20 min, continuing to the downtown river mouth), and the Beach Line (South Beach ↔ Brickell, 20–25 min). Phase 2 adds a north-bay group — Sunset Harbour, Edgewater, Downtown/Bayside, the Upper Eastside, and Bal Harbour — rendered as planned, not promised. Miami and Fort Lauderdale operate as two independent networks. There is no boat between them — Brightline already does that trip in about 35 minutes, and we won't pretend water beats rail there.
copy.network_footnote: Miami and Fort Lauderdale operate as two independent networks. There is no boat between them — Brightline already does that trip in about 35 minutes, and we won't pretend water beats rail there. Aventura joins as a summer-season station (May–mid-November): the Intracoastal channel there is a slow-speed manatee-protection zone from November 15 to April 30, so foil-speed service pauses each winter. We'd rather tell you that now than surprise you later. Fort Lauderdale is its own network: the Hollywood Commuter (Hollywood Beach ↔ 17th St ↔ downtown Riverwalk) and the Isles Shuttle (Bahia Mar ↔ Riverwalk) put the Las Olas office spine and the county government center a short walk from the dock. Fort Lauderdale's beloved Water Taxi runs 10 AM to 10 PM — we serve the commuter hours it doesn't, as a complement, not a competitor.
